selected_evidence.requirement: Every command run through sudo is recorded with user and timestamp
selected_evidence.summary: sudo-commands.log contains lines like 'Sep 4 23:46:42 node1 sudo[1662]: testsudo : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/whoami' and a post-reboot entry for user root, showing timestamp, invoking user, and command captured.

selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log and secure log
selected_evidence.summary: grep for sudo COMMAND= lines in /var/log/messages returns 0 matches both before and after reboot; the only 3 matches in /var/log/secure are timestamped at 23:45:03/10:26:56, before the local2 logging config was applied at ~23:46, confirming no post-configuration leakage into either general log.

selected_evidence.requirement: Configuration mechanism (syslog facility routing) is correct and persistent
selected_evidence.summary: sudo configured to log to syslog facility local2 via validated sudoers.d drop-in; rsyslog.d/00-sudo-commands.conf routes local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with stop; confirmed rsyslog.d includes load before the messages/secure catch-all rules; config verified present and unchanged after restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured on node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07), rsyslog active status, sudoers/rsyslog config contents, and existing log contents before restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection, restart actually occurs
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately; subsequent poll still succeeded briefly then a poll returned connection timed out, showing the node went down for restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed after restart (proof of actual restart)
selected_evidence.summary: boot_id changed from bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07 to d8113afa-ba47-4fbc-b86a-252ecf1c4317, and uptime -s shows a new boot time (23:47:10), proving the kernel actually restarted.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required service/config/data
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, rsyslog is active, sudoers.d and rsyslog.d config files are intact, prior log entries persisted, and a new sudo command issued post-restart was correctly captured only in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with zero leakage into /var/log/messages, confirming full functional recovery.
